findings.text: the ruff figures in evidence_inputs are transposed and do not reproduce. The manifest reads "base 1 finding / 0 would-reformat, head 1 finding / 0 would-reformat"; measured with the repository's own config and --no-cache in each arm, ruff check reports 'All checks passed!' in both, i.e. 0 findings, while ruff format --check reports '1 file would be reformatted' in both. The two labels appear to have been swapped - the 1 belongs to would-reformat and the 0 to check findings. Nothing substantive turns on it: the requirement the figures support, that the change adds no ruff finding against base, holds either way because both arms read the same in both instruments, and I confirmed that zero delta directly. The repair is to swap the labels so a later reader who reruns the command gets what the record says.

item_verdicts.call_sites: the fix sits at the single funnel every live-pointer write already passes through - runs.py:_write_json calling _stamp_pointer_launch_host at :396. Ten _write_json(pointer_path(...)) call sites route through it across four modules (claims.py, dispatch.py, promotion.py, resumption.py, plus runs.py itself), so no pointer writer is left uncovered and no writer needed editing.
item_verdicts.diff: read the single commit 8ab1f3c7 against its parent 6d528821 (34 insertions, 7 deletions, one file). It splits the old first-write-only stamp into a read-back helper _recorded_launch_host and a carry-forward branch: a payload already naming the key is returned untouched; a path outside live_dir() is returned untouched; an existing live pointer inherits the host its own file already names, and is left alone when it names none; only a file being created is stamped with socket.gethostname(). No signature, no caller and no other file moved, and the new branch is the whole of the product change.
item_verdicts.done_when: met. The target id is red at base and green at head; the head arm adds no failing id; tests/test_a_foreign_pid_never_reads_dead.py passes in both arms and tests/test_a_live_run_never_reads_dead.py keeps its one pre-existing red unchanged. Both arms are delivered as one JSON object each under baseline_suite and after_suite carrying revision, command, exit_status, log_path and failure_ids, and I checked each declared failure_ids list for set equality against its own log's FAILED lines - 18 of 18 at base and 17 of 17 at head, so the record's ids are the logs' ids and not a paraphrase. The manifest names the attributing commit in failure_attribution, as the done-when required, with the isolation measurements at 58405bd6 (EXIT=0) and b0809e30 (EXIT=1). The negative control reverts the one change in a scratch copy of the head and repeats the declared string verbatim on its first line.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal was the red id tests/test_crew.py::test_live_view_rechecks_a_killed_worker_without_observation, and the node chose correctly between the two branches the dispatch offered. It did not give the fixture a host: tests/test_crew.py is byte-identical across base..head (git diff --quiet 6d528821 8ab1f3c7 -- tests/test_crew.py reports no change) and the whole commit is reckon/crew/runs.py, 34 insertions and 7 deletions. It restored the lost path in production instead, which is the branch that treats the red id as a real defect rather than a stale fixture. The attribution is correct and I verified it independently: b0809e30 "a foreign pid is not a death on the reading host" (merge 8413ce50be905f074613803ef2a63b09f654b5c6) touches recovery.py, runs.py and tests/test_a_foreign_pid_never_reads_dead.py and introduces the three launcher_host lines in recovery.py; the test function carries 2 asserts at 58405bd6, b0809e30, 6d528821 and head, so the code moved and the test did not.
item_verdicts.manifest: read in full at 46 lines, and deliberately read late. The first read, taken while the reviewed process was still running, caught a 17-line intermediate whose baseline_suite carried only revision and command, whose baseline_suite command held an unsubstituted tests/test_a_foreign_pid_<placeholder>, and which had no after_suite key at all; the delivered 46-line record written at 13:55:23, five minutes before the process exited at 13:57:32, carries both arms complete, a five-paragraph failure_attribution, a negative_control_note describing the scratch construction, and the ruff figures. That ordering is the contract's own durable-write pattern (write what you hold, then improve it), not a defect, and the review is recorded against the delivered state. One accuracy defect survives in it, carried below as the single finding. The node reports in its reply that it ran about eight minutes past its 60-minute fence finishing and validating the manifest; the manifest does not record the overrun. No measurement was affected and the disclosure is the fence's own remedy, so it is noted here rather than scored as a defect.
item_verdicts.write_paths: five paths were granted (reckon/crew/runs.py, reckon/crew/recovery.py, tests/test_crew.py and one evidence fragment plus a figure directory under docs/); the commit touches exactly reckon/crew/runs.py, inside the grant, and git status --porcelain -uno on the worktree is empty. Four of the five grants are unused: the evidence fragment and the figure directory were never written, and recovery.py and tests/test_crew.py were correctly left alone, which is the point of the node's answer to the goal.

justifications.durability: the guard fails exactly under the regression it exists to catch and holds under inputs the run did not try. Removing the one change reddens the target id, which is the run's own negative control. I then probed the carry with four pointer populations (/tmp/hostcheck/check_foreign_guard.py) and at head all four hold: a fresh keyless pointer takes the writing host; a payload naming a foreign host keeps it; an existing pointer naming a foreign host keeps that host rather than gaining the rewriter's; and a pointer naming no host at all gains none. At base the third case fails, so the fix is strictly better than what it replaces and does not reopen the foreign-pid defect by inventing a local host - which is exactly the failure a naive 'always stamp the rewriter's host' repair would have introduced. The ten pointer-write call sites all funnel through the one patched function, and the residual - a pointer written before the key existed stays unproven - is disclosed under follow_ons rather than hidden.
justifications.evidence: the evidence is strong and I re-derived it rather than trusting it. Both arms name revision, tree, full command, module.__file__ and cwd on their header lines and end in an EXIT= line; I extracted the FAILED ids from both logs myself and both declared lists match their logs exactly, 18 of 18 and 17 of 17, giving added_failure_count 0 and added_failure_ids empty with the single removed id being the target. The instrument is shown to see failures rather than nothing - it reports 17 and 18 of them - so a zero delta is a measurement, not a blind instrument. The negative control is genuine: line 1 repeats the declared string verbatim and the target fails there with assert True is False at tests/test_crew.py:3145. I also ran the harness's own derivation (reckon.crew.review.annotate_review_of_run) against the delivered manifest and it resolves both gate logs by field name and returns 0 with an empty id list, agreeing with my derivation. One figure pair does not reproduce, and it is the single finding below; the requirement it belongs to - no added ruff finding against base - is itself confirmed, so the defect is in the label rather than the result.
justifications.fit: the commit carries a conventional subject and a body that states the two-write sequence causing the drop, with no trailer, no plan label and no ticket reference; the helper _recorded_launch_host is named for what it returns and sits beside the function it serves; the docstring states the mechanism and the reason rather than the change history, and the failure_attribution block reads from the code at each named commit rather than from a bisect, which is what the dispatch asked for. The blemishes are small: a hard-wrapped fragment in the rewritten docstring ('has no recoverable launching' ends a line and the next begins 'host,'), and the fence overrun noted under the manifest verdict.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the required behaviour landed and I reproduced its mechanism independently rather than resting on the run's own log. Writing a claim pointer that names the host and then a record pointer that does not - the exact two-write sequence a dispatch performs - leaves the key present at head and absent at base (/tmp/hostcheck/check_host_carry.py: base /tmp/lvk-base prints DROPPED, the worktree prints PRESERVED, and record_replaced_claim reads true, so the second write really did replace the file). I confirmed the node did not take the easier fixture branch, and I confirmed the attribution commit, its merge, its touched files and the constant assertion count of 2 across all four revisions.
justifications.scope_discipline: exemplary. One commit, one file, inside the declared grant, staged explicitly; the worktree is clean; the granted evidence fragment and figure directory were not written and nothing outside the grant was touched; the test file the goal tempted a weaker node to edit was left byte-identical; no plan state, index or sprint file was touched.
